items.answer: Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.
Mixed reality (MR) is an immersive technology that is the same as augmented reality, in which digital content is overlaid on the view of reality and can be interacted with.

Reality-virtuality continuum is a scale whose extremes are a completely real environment with nothing virtual and a completely virtual environment with nothing real, with augmented reality and augmented virtuality as intermediate states between them.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

Virtual environment is a non-real, computer-generated graphical representation of a real or imaginary world, populated with artificial objects, that is experienced through computer-generated sensory stimuli.

questions.question: In the systemic definition, what must a system that combines the real world with virtual content and supports real-time interaction also do to qualify as augmented reality?
options: Register the virtual content in 3D
Replace the real view with a fully virtual environment
Keep the virtual content fixed to the display screen
Let the user choose a separate location for the virtual content
questions.explanation: The systemic definition requires an AR system to combine the real world with virtual content, be interactive in real time, and be registered in 3D. Replacing the real view or fixing content to a screen does not satisfy that 3D registration requirement.

questions.question: What does it mean that an augmented reality system supports interaction with the digital content in the enhanced environment rather than separately?
options: The user points to the content with a physical marker
The user interacts with it while remaining in the real world
The user controls the real-world view but not the digital content
The user switches to a separate application to touch the content
questions.explanation: One AR characteristic is that interaction with the digital content happens within the enhanced environment, giving the user the feel of being in reality at all times. A separate application or separate control channel breaks that continuity.

questions.question: What follows from the rule that an augmented reality system is identified only by checking the four AR characteristics one by one?
options: A system that fails one characteristic is still an AR system if the interaction is real time
A system that fails one characteristic is still an AR system if the content is visible
A system that fails one characteristic is not an AR system
A system that fails one characteristic is still an AR system if the other three are satisfied
questions.explanation: Under the four-characteristic test, all four characteristics must be satisfied for a system to be an AR system. If at least one is missing, the system is not an AR system, regardless of how well the others are met.

data.text: Augmented reality is a technology-enhanced view in which digital information is placed over the real world. A systemic definition leads to a practical recognition test built from four characteristics. A system qualifies as augmented reality only when all four characteristics are present.
points: Augmented reality is technology-created enhanced reality that overlays digital information on an image viewed through a device.
A systemic augmented reality definition requires real-world/virtual combination, real-time interaction, and 3D registration.
An augmented reality system has four characteristics: computer-generated enhancement, 3D registration, sensory experience, and interaction in the enhanced environment.
A system is augmented reality only if it satisfies all four augmented reality characteristics; one missing disqualifies it.

questions.question: How do augmented reality and virtual reality differ in their treatment of reality?
options: AR creates a virtual environment, while VR retains it
AR alters the ongoing perception of the real world, while VR replaces it
VR alters the ongoing perception of the real world, while AR replaces it
AR removes the need for a physical place, while VR preserves it
questions.explanation: Augmented reality changes how the real world is perceived, whereas virtual reality substitutes a virtual environment for the user's sense of reality. The reversed option and the virtual-environment option put the VR property onto AR.

questions.question: What does an augmented or mixed reality system require that a virtual reality system does not?
options: the place being experienced to exist
the place being experienced to be virtual
the real-world view to be removed
the user's sense of reality to be replaced
questions.explanation: Augmented and mixed reality experiences depend on a real place existing, while virtual reality can create its environment without that place. Replacing the user's sense of reality or removing the real-world view belongs to virtual reality, not AR or MR.

questions.question: How can an augmented reality system show non-existent furniture in a real room?
options: By removing the furniture from the user's sense of the room
By superimposing it as digital content on the room
By replacing the room with a virtual version of the room
By requiring the furniture to be physically present in the room
questions.explanation: An AR system can overlay digital content, such as non-existent furniture, on the real room as the user sees it. Replacing or removing the room would change the real world rather than augment it.

data.text: Augmented reality and virtual reality differ in how they treat the real world. Virtual reality creates a virtual environment that replaces the user's sense of reality and does not need a real object or place. Augmented or mixed reality requires an existing real place, and augmented reality can add digital content over the user's real-world perception.
points: Augmented reality alters ongoing real-world perception, whereas virtual reality completely replaces the user's sense of reality.
A virtual reality system needs no physical object or place, while augmented or mixed reality requires the place to exist.
An augmented reality system can superimpose extra information as digital content over a real-world room view.

questions.question: What characterizes the precise definition of mixed reality across professional and academic sources?
options: agreement on a fixed developer definition
agreement on a categorical dictionary definition
agreement on a settled continuum definition
no agreement on one precise definition
questions.explanation: Mixed reality has no single agreed precise definition. Dictionary, developer, and continuum views are alternative accounts, not one settled meaning.

questions.question: Where does augmented reality belong under the continuum definition of mixed reality?
options: at the virtual end of the reality-virtuality continuum
within the mixed-reality range of the reality-virtuality continuum
at the real end of the reality-virtuality continuum
outside the mixed-reality range of the reality-virtuality continuum
questions.explanation: The continuum definition treats mixed reality as the space between the real and virtual extremes, so augmented reality is included inside that range.

questions.question: From a developer's point of view, what kind of capability does mixed reality denote?
options: a combined augmented-reality and virtual-reality capability
a synonymous augmented-reality and virtual-reality capability
a continuum augmented-reality and virtual-reality capability
a stronger augmented-reality plus virtual-reality capability
questions.explanation: In the developer view, mixed reality denotes the ability to combine augmented-reality and virtual-reality technology in the same application or device. Strong augmented reality, continuum placement, and simple digital overlay are different definitions or related properties.

questions.question: What does the 'strong version of augmented reality' definition emphasize about mixed reality?
options: an advanced replacement of the physical environment
an advanced overlay of digital content on the environment
an advanced interaction with digital content in the environment
an advanced understanding of the physical environment
questions.explanation: In this definition, mixed reality is a more capable form of augmented reality with a stronger understanding of the physical environment. Overlay and interaction describe augmented-reality features, while replacement points toward virtual reality.

data.text: Mixed reality has no single accepted definition, and a dictionary description does not clearly separate it from augmented or virtual reality. Some definitions broaden it, treating it as the whole space between real and virtual environments or as a capability to combine augmented and virtual reality in one application or device. Other definitions narrow it to augmented reality, as a stronger form or a synonym, so the course avoids the confusion by treating mixed reality and augmented reality as the same technology.
points: Mixed reality lacks an agreed precise definition, and its dictionary definition does not distinguish it from VR or AR.
One definition treats mixed reality as everything between real and virtual environments, so it includes augmented reality.
Another definition says mixed reality means combining augmented and virtual reality in one application or device.
Some definitions call mixed reality stronger augmented reality or a synonym for augmented reality with overlaid, interactive digital content.
In this course, mixed reality is treated as the same technology as augmented reality, so the terms are interchangeable.

questions.question: What does the course assume about the relationship between mixed reality and augmented reality?
options: Mixed reality is assumed to be the combination of virtual and augmented technologies
Mixed reality is assumed to be a span across the reality-virtuality continuum
Mixed reality is assumed to be the same technology as augmented reality
Mixed reality is assumed to be a stronger version of augmented reality
questions.explanation: The course treats mixed reality and augmented reality as interchangeable, adopting the common practitioner view for simplicity. The other options describe alternative definitions of mixed reality rather than the course's assumed relationship.

data.text: The course adopts a simplifying convention: mixed reality is treated as the same technology and idea as augmented reality. This makes the later discussion simpler.
points: In this course, mixed reality is assumed to be the same technology and idea as augmented reality.

options: Supporting interaction in the enhanced environment
Enhancing the real world with digital content
Replacing the user's sense of reality
Registering the enhancement in 3D
items.reason: The three are characteristics of an augmented reality system, whereas replacing the user's sense of reality is what virtual reality does.

questions.question: What does the position of augmented reality and virtual reality on the reality-virtuality continuum imply about whether the experienced place must exist?
questions.reference_answer: Augmented reality requires the place being experienced to exist, while virtual reality does not require a physical object or place. On the reality-virtuality continuum, augmented reality is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content, while virtual reality replaces the user's sense of reality with a virtual environment.

questions.question: How does checking the four augmented reality characteristics distinguish an augmented reality system from a system that only displays digital content?
questions.reference_answer: The four characteristics make an all-or-nothing identification test: a system must enhance the real world with digital content, register that enhancement in three dimensions, provide it through the user's sensory organs, and support interaction with the content in the enhanced environment. If any one is missing, the system is not an augmented reality system, so merely displaying digital content is insufficient.

questions.question: Why are mixed reality and augmented reality treated as interchangeable in the course?
questions.reference_answer: Because definitions of mixed reality are not agreed and the resulting controversy is not needed for the course, the course assumes mixed reality is the same technology and idea as augmented reality. It therefore treats the two terms as interchangeable in its later discussion.
